title: Any 3D Scene is Worth 1K Tokens: 3D-Grounded Representation for Scene Generation at Scale
claim: A fixed-length implicit 3D latent lets one encoder-decoder and a diffusion model generate consistent scenes quickly under varied conditioning.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right flow, gallery of generated scenes below
description: The figure has two stacked panels split by a dashed line. Panel (a) is a left-to-right pipeline. Multi-view photos with camera icons go into a blue 3DRAE Encoder, labelled as a frozen 2D encoder. This produces green fixed-length 3D latent tokens. A blue decoder takes those tokens together with purple novel-view pose queries. It outputs decoded images, colored point maps and a colored 3D point cloud. Panel (b) repeats the flow for generation. Conditional images and a trajectory go through the encoder and become orange conditional tokens. Gray noisy tokens join them as input to a teal 3DDiT block. The 3DDiT outputs green generated tokens, which the decoder turns into images and point maps. A light-blue banner reads 'Scenes Generated in 2s'. Below it, three point-cloud scenes show unconditional, single-view and sparse-view generation. Yellow camera and '?' boxes mark which views are given.
caption: 3D-Grounded Scene Generation. (a) Our 3DRAE repurposes frozen 2D foundation models to ground varying number of views into fixed-length implicit 3D latent tokens, which can be queried to decode images and point maps of various views including novel views. (b) Our 3DDiT performs diffusion modeling directly in this implicit 3D latent space, enabling 3D-grounded generation with superior efficiency and spatial consistency.
abstract: Scene-level 3D generation has long been dominated by 2D multi-view or video diffusion models. Typically, these 2D-based approaches perform scene generation in a 2D latent space, which introduces two fundamental issues: (i) representing 3D scenes via 2D views leads to significant representation redundancy, and (ii) latent space rooted in 2D inherently limits the spatial consistency of the generated scenes. In this paper, we propose to perform 3D scene generation directly within a high-dimensional implicit 3D latent space derived from powerful 2D foundation models (e.g., DINOv2, SigLIP2, DA3). Then we tame diffusion transformers to perform diffusion modeling directly in the 3D latent space, enabling 3D-grounded scene generation. In our experiments, we not only demonstrate the advantages of our method over 2D-based approaches in terms of efficiency and spatial consistency, but also comprehensively analyze the impact of 3D latent representation on 3D scene generation performance. Furthermore, we validate the favorable scalability of our method with respect to representation and model capacity.
